/kind bug
<!--

/kind feature

/kind deprecation
/kind failing-test
/kind flake
/kind regression
-->

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Return a typed error that also passes as a "Missing Version Error"
so that server side apply updates are not blocked from happening on
custom resources that have a version that is no longer available.

This commit also adds an integration test to verify the same.

> This issue is biting us pretty hard in Cluster API, is there any chance to backport this to older releases of Kubernetes (as much as possible?)

It's too early to comment about the possibility of backports, but my inclination would be not to backport, since this isn't a regression (and the implications are super hard to reason about).

issue_context.title: managedField entry for a removed API version prevent further resource updates
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

Hi - a user reported an issue were server-side apply (ssa) stopped working.  

ref: https://github.com/knative/operator/issues/1184

Server-side apply works on resources as CRD versions are deprecated and removed.

@apelisse While this would avoid the immediate issue, I wonder if that fully addresses the problem. Is the expected behavior that managedFields for already removed apiVersions just remain?

We've hit the same issue in Cluster API, while it would be nice to not hit the issue in SSA we also don't feel very comfortable with just ignoring the managedFields for removed apiVersions. So we're considering implementing some sort of garbage collector which removes managedFields for apiVersions that have been already removed.

But before implementing this "downstream" in Cluster API, I'm wondering how other folks are handling this / what the best practice is. I would expect that a lot of folks are hitting this issue with CRDs as soon as they try to remove apiVersions.

I would imagine that if we just ignore the managedFields for removed apiVersions we collect a considerable amount of garbage over time.

Just for reference. The current issue makes it pretty hard / very hacky to remove apiVersions from CRDs.

When a CRD has multiple apiVersions (even if they are unused and not served) we are getting a lot of conversion requests. More details in: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/129979

I did some more tests related to this issue.

Let's assume we do the following:
* Deploy a CRD with v1alpha3 + v1beta1 (storage version)
* Deploy a corresponding CR with v1alpha3 (this will lead to a v1alpha3 entry in managedFields)
* Update the CRD to only contain v1beta1

At this point we have a CR which still has a v1alpha3 managedField entry

Now one of the following things might happen

Option 1: kubectl apply with server-side=true

* kubectl will print an error like this: `request to convert CR to an invalid group/version: cluster.x-k8s.io/v1alpha3`
* apiserver will print an error like this:
> E0207 13:34:58.510654       1 status.go:71] "Unhandled Error" err="apiserver received an error that is not an metav1.Status: &errors.errorString{s:\"request to convert CR to an invalid group/version: [cluster.x-k8s.io/v1alpha3](http://cluster.x-k8s.io/v1alpha3)\"}: request to convert CR to an invalid group/version: [cluster.x-k8s.io/v1alpha3](http://cluster.x-k8s.io/v1alpha3)" logger="UnhandledError"

Option 2: kubectl apply without server-side

* kubectl apply will go through, but managedFields will be gone (can be observed via `kubectl get`, object looks the same in etcd)
* apiserver will print an error like this:
> [SHOULD NOT HAPPEN] failed to update managedFields" err="failed to update ManagedFields (default/capi-quickstart; [cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1](http://cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1), Kind=Cluster): request to convert CR to an invalid group/version: [cluster.x-k8s.io/v1alpha3](http://cluster.x-k8s.io/v1alpha3)" versionKind="[cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1](http://cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1), Kind=Cluster" namespace="default" name="capi-quickstart

If now kubectl apply with server-side=true is run, managedFields show up again (obviously the field doesn't have the same content as before we lost it)


So I think the situation "fixes" itself if updates with and without server-side are applied on the object, while probably (?) losing previous field ownership information.

(btw not sure if #115650 addresses option 2)


One question. I assume once an apiVersion is not served anymore it should not be possible to get new managedField entries for that apiVersion? (trying to figure out a way to deal with the current state :))

Just in case it's useful to anyone. Here's an issue summarizing what we are doing in Cluster API now before we remove an apiVersion: https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/cluster-api/issues/11894 (also summarizes the current challenges around apiVersion removal)

@jpbetz the reason for this is in how the `notRegisteredErr` string is formatted here: https://github.com/MadhavJivrajani/kubernetes/blob/fa6dcc734bf6d6faa720714628b8709c27736f19/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/runtime/error.go#L73

There are two main cases to take care of: when we use a `genericContext` and when we use a `schemeContext`. If the `genericContext` is used (meaning we already know what the scheme is, such as in cases of built in types), things would be okay for the most part, however, if we use a `schemeContext` (for when we don't know the scheme before hand such as in CRs), we need to add in a ` in scheme ` there towards the _end_ of the formatted `notRegisteredErr` error string. So to handle both cases and not overcomplicate the formatting logic, a space is padded here.
